item.title: [DIS] Twine — Non-Custodial P2P for Nervos CKB on Nostr and Fiber (1 posts)
item.description: About half an hour after the discussion-phase result was announced (Nov 24, 18:21 UTC+8), a community member asked about several new accounts that liked this proposal on the final day of the window. I reviewed the likes with forum admin data. Three of the liking accounts were registered from one network address within five hours, and each liked within 81 seconds of registering. Nothing in the data links them to the proposal author. Under the practice of t/7707 and t/10453, their likes would be removed, which would leave 29 of the announced 32, one short of the threshold. item.title: Oracell: Contention-Free Witness Oracle for Nervos CKB (Phase 1 MVP Live on Pudge — Feedback Welcome) (1 posts)
item.description: Hi everyone, I’ve been working on Oracell, a contention-free oracle infrastructure built natively for Nervos CKB’s Cell Model as part of the CKB Builder Track (Week 11–12). Following initial architecture discussions, Phase 1 (MVP) is now live on Pudge Testnet (rikokurnia/oracell on GitHub, live app at oracell [dot] vercel [dot] app), and I’d love to gather technical feedback from the wider CKB community before moving into Phase 2. item.title: Community Fund DAO voting in numbers (2 posts)
item.description: 1信息获取渠道应该是一个很大的问题，渠道太过分散，关注Dao的X账户的人很少，在talk论坛中注册并定期查看信息的更少。 2无法用移动终端进行投票也是一个关键问题。登录桌面钱包等待信息更新，再跳转几个网站，操作很麻烦。 3相关提案与社区成员的利益关系不大，且很多提案技术性较强，很多成员觉得通过与不通过都没有关系，除了个别资金量大或者争议性大的项目，倾向于不投票，让其他人决定。 4已通过Dao资助项目的履约情况以及后续的持续运营也是一个非常大的因素。Nervos上太多项目开发完以后就被束之高阁，被开发者放弃了。现在缺少真正一个从Dao资助出来一个成功的案例，尤其是Dao里面很多宣传或者活动，很难让人信服能产生什么长期有效的效果。

item.title: Design Patterns: UTXO Transfers Using the Cell Model (2 posts)
item.description: How to transfer assets with the Cell Model is a surprisingly complex subject because of the state rent requirements. We wanted to share a guide on seven patterns (both current and future) that developers should understand. Design Patterns: UTXO Transfers Using the Cell Model This document explores different patterns for transferring digital assets between two parties using the Nervos CKB Cell Model. While focused on the CKB blockchain, these patterns may also apply to other UTXO blockchains that implement state rent. State rent is essential because it ensures sustainable network economics and prevents out of control cost spirals. However, it introduces unique challenges that require...

item.title: Understanding CKB Lock Value Relationships (2 posts)
item.description: When you work with the CKB Cell Model, there are a lot of different lock values and the terminology can be confusing at first. Even for a seasoned developer, how all these values fit together is often overlooked. This is why we are sharing this guide to explain it in simple terms. Understanding CKB Lock Value Relationships In CKB smart contract development, it is important to understand how different lock-related values connect to each other. These values form a chain of cryptographic relationships that are used throughout smart contract development for purposes such as ownership verification, address generation, and cross-referencing between different scripts. item.title: Using the CKBHash Function in CKB Development (2 posts)
item.description: CKBHash is a term you might see within the various CKB libraries, and for basic usage it’s abstracted away for you. For more advanced lock design you need to understand what it is and where it is commonly applied. We put together a quick guide to explain how these conventions work. Using the CKBHash Function in CKB Development When building smart contracts on CKB you are free to use any cryptographic function that you wish to use. However, many of the system scripts and within the commonly used libraries rely on Blake2b.
